tharavad

tharavad (tharavadu) is malayalam for the ancestral home. the big old house where the whole extended family lives. that's the model. not a product with a login page. a house with keys.

what

one server in a hackerspace in kerala. you open a pull request, someone reads it, you get a linux machine with your name on it.

  • ssh you@you.tharavad.xyz from anywhere
  • root on your own nixos vm. your mess stays yours
  • a port in git → https://you.tharavad.xyz

no signup form. no credit card. no ticket. join.

why

most people who wanted a box at 13 never got one. signup walls, cards, "contact sales". the useful rooms closed when the forums did. we can't fix that. we can keep one house open.

renting teaches you someone's billing page. owning teaches you watts, disks, packets, boot order. that stuff is true everywhere. and when you can't buy more compute, you write better code.

git is the guest list. your access is a file in a public repo. who's in, who let them in, when, why: git log. no secret admin list. no favours.

break it. nothing in here is precious. the whole house builds from one repo, so when it falls over we put it back and time how long that took. then we make the number smaller.

how

a used dell r730xd. 88 threads, 62 GB, 151 W idle. one small vps in front as the door. the space's firewall. all of it is one nix flake: tinkerhub0/mothership. the docs are written for people who've never done this before.

tinkerhub bought the iron. we run it.
